prompt:
I need the front end for Replay Room. An in-house library built by a large bank's platform engineering department to store recorded incident review meetings, with transcripts and links to the systems and runbooks discussed, so engineers can study past outages.

Who's using it: Farah Siddiqui, a site reliability engineer who transferred from the mobile app team to the core payments platform group a month ago. She starts her first on-call rotation Monday. Her manager has asked her to watch the past two quarters' major incident reviews before then. She's going through them at her desk on a quiet Friday afternoon with headphones on.

What they're doing right now: She's 23 minutes into the 52-minute review of last August's payments ledger replication lag incident. The first stretch was timeline recap she already read in the written postmortem, and she wants to jump to where the database lead explains why the automatic failover didn't trigger. She'd like to watch that part at 1.5x, rewind to catch a command someone read aloud, and bookmark the moment for her runbook notes. After that she needs to decide which review to watch next. Two others involve the same replication cluster, and she has about two hours left today with nine required reviews still unwatched.

What's in the system at this point: 46 recorded incident reviews from Jan 2025 to Oct 2026, each 25–75 minutes long. Each has a severity (SEV1–SEV3), affected services, date, facilitator, participants with speaker labels, a full timestamped transcript, chapter markers (e.g., 'Detection', 'Failover attempt', 'Customer impact', 'Action items'), and links to the written postmortem, runbooks and tickets. Farah's required onboarding playlist has 14 reviews: 5 watched, 1 in progress at 23:10 of 52:04, and 8 untouched. Her personal bookmarks include 6 timestamps with notes. Related-incident links show that 'INC-2026-0812 ledger replication lag' shares the cluster pg-ledger-east-02 with INC-2026-0419 and INC-2025-1130.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
